opinions: The statement 'AI is currently just glorified compression' captures a provocative but limited perspective on current AI, particularly generative models like large language models (LLMs).
Learning involves compressing data into useful representations.
Modern LLMs are trained to predict the next token, which can be seen as compressing vast training data into model weights.
AI models generate outputs based on patterns in training data—they don't create truly novel information outside their training distribution.
AI models are 'recompressing' existing knowledge.
Models sometimes reproduce training examples verbatim, highlighting their role as advanced pattern-matching systems rather than reasoning entities.
Modern AI demonstrates emergent abilities (e.g., reasoning across domains, solving unseen problems) that go beyond simple compression.
Models can combine concepts in novel ways not present in training data.
AI systems can engage in real-time dialogue, adjust responses based on context, and even exhibit creativity—behaviors not typical of static compression algorithms.
Compression reduces data size while preserving information, but AI aims for understanding—grasping semantics, intent, and context.
A compressed file doesn't answer questions; an AI does.
